OBJETO DEL PUESTO El/la Técnico/a de Proyectos se encargará, bajo la coordinación del Área de Proyectos, del seguimiento y gestión técnica de las intervenciones que le sean asignadas, asegurando su adecuada ejecución, el cumplimiento de los compromisos adquiridos con los financiadores y la calidad de la documentación técnica y de seguimiento. Asimismo, participará en la identificación y formulación de nuevas propuestas de financiación, en la relación con los equipos de terreno y socios locales y en los procesos de aprendizaje y mejora continua de las intervenciones de PSF. 3. PRINCIPALES FUNCIONES Y RESPONSABILIDADES 3.1. Identificación y formulación de proyectos Identificar oportunidades de financiación y nuevas propuestas de intervención en coordinación con el Área de Proyectos y los equipos de terreno. Analizar convocatorias y requisitos de los diferentes financiadores, especialmente de la cooperación pública española y de la Unión Europea. Participar en la identificación, diseño y formulación de proyectos y programas de cooperación internacional y acción humanitaria. Revisar y mejorar propuestas elaboradas conjuntamente con los equipos de terreno y socios locales. Participar en la elaboración de marcos lógicos, cronogramas, presupuestos, indicadores y sistemas de seguimiento. 3.2. Seguimiento técnico de proyectos Realizar el seguimiento técnico de los proyectos asignados durante todo su ciclo de ejecución. Supervisar el cumplimiento de actividades, resultados, indicadores y objetivos previstos. Analizar periódicamente el grado de avance de las intervenciones y detectar desviaciones, riesgos o necesidades de adaptación. Acompañar a los equipos de terreno en la planificación, ejecución y seguimiento de las actividades. Realizar visitas periódicas a los países de intervención cuando sea necesario para el adecuado seguimiento de los proyectos. 3.3. Informes y relación con financiadores Elaborar y/o coordinar la elaboración de informes técnicos de seguimiento y finales de los proyectos asignados. Revisar la documentación técnica y económica necesaria para la justificación de las intervenciones. Preparar comunicaciones y solicitudes dirigidas a los financiadores relacionadas con la gestión de los proyectos. Participar en reuniones con financiadores y otros actores institucionales cuando corresponda. 3.4. Coordinación interna Mantener una comunicación fluida y periódica con los equipos de terreno y las delegaciones de PSF. Participar en las reuniones de coordinación del Área de Proyectos. Coordinarse con las áreas administrativa y financiera y con el resto de áreas de la organización cuando sea necesario. Representar a PSF en foros, redes y espacios relacionados con los proyectos cuando sea requerido. 4. PERFIL REQUERIDO Formación Titulación universitaria, preferentemente en ámbitos relacionados con el puesto de trabajo ofertado. Formación especializada, máster o posgrado en cooperación internacional para el desarrollo, acción humanitaria, gestión de proyectos o ámbitos relacionados, pudiendo suplirse este requisito con experiencia de trabajo contrastada en organizaciones de cooperación internacional.  Experiencia profesional Experiencia mínima de 2 años en puestos relacionados con la gestión de proyectos de cooperación internacional. Experiencia demostrable en identificación, formulación, seguimiento y justificación de proyectos. Experiencia en gestión de proyectos financiados por administraciones públicas españolas (AECID, AACID y otras agencias de cooperación españolas) Se valorará experiencia con financiación de la Unión Europea u otros organismos internacionales.  Conocimientos técnicos Conocimiento del ciclo de gestión de proyectos de cooperación internacional, marco lógico y gestión basada en resultados. Capacidad para realizar seguimiento técnico y presupuestario de proyectos. Excelente capacidad de redacción de documentos técnicos e informes. Capacidad de análisis de convocatorias y normativa de financiadores. Buen manejo de herramientas ofimáticas, especialmente Microsoft Office Se valorará experiencia con herramientas de seguimiento de proyectos. Idiomas Castellano: nivel alto, oral y escrito. Inglés: nivel medio.  Francés: nivel medio-alto 5. DEPENDENCIA Y RELACIONES El/la Técnico/a de Proyectos desarrollará su actividad dentro del Área de Proyectos de PSF, bajo la coordinación y dependencia funcional de la persona responsable del área. 6. CONDICIONES DEL PUESTO Lugar de trabajo: Málaga Modalidad: presencial, con base en la oficina de PSF en Málaga Jornada: completa. Tipo de contrato: según la legislación laboral española y las condiciones establecidas por PSF. Retribución: según el baremo salarial establecido por PSF para el puesto. Viajes: disponibilidad para realizar dos o tres viajes de forma anual a los países de intervención cuando las necesidades de los proyectos lo requieran. Incorporación prevista: inicio de diciembre de 2026. 7. PROCESO DE SELECCIÓN El proceso de selección se desarrollará de acuerdo con los principios de igualdad de oportunidades, no discriminación y transparencia. El proceso incluirá entrevista personal, pudiendo incluir:  Prueba técnica relacionada con las funciones del puesto. Entrevista final con las personas responsables de la organización, cuando corresponda. Únicamente se contactará con las candidaturas que pasen a las siguientes fases del proceso. 8. PRESENTACIÓN DE CANDIDATURAS Las personas interesadas deberán enviar: CV actualizado. Carta de motivación. Las candidaturas deberán remitirse a: info@pozossinfronteras.org Indicando en el asunto: “Técnico/a de Proyectos – Sede Málaga” Plazo de presentación de candidaturas: hasta el 15 de noviembre de 2026. (este plazo podrá ser ampliado).  La incorporación está prevista para inicio de diciembre de 2026.

review_candidates.description: Job Description Grade: E Deadline: 22 November 2026 (11:59 PM KST) Introduction The Green Climate Fund is the world’s largest dedicated multilateral climate fund and invests in impactful, innovative, catalytic programs and projects in developing countries across the globe.The GCF has a portfolio of 379 projects across 137 countries, with a total commitment of USD 22.3 billion to date. In 2023, an additional USD 12.8 billion was pledged, to support our new strategic and programming cycle from 2024-2027; our ambition is to grow to become at least a USD 50 billion fund by 2030. Rooted in the core objectives of impact and efficiency, access and a focus on the most vulnerable, and mobilizing a much higher scale of public and private sector financial flows for climate action we have an unparalleled scale of resources, which, together with our risk appetite and flexibility allows us to bring together different partners and stakeholders in innovative partnerships for profound impact. GCF is seeking a top-tier individual with a demonstrable track record of harnessing experience, energy and networks to tackle complex global climate change challenges. You will be committed to making a positive, measurable difference through a mission-driven role, and thrive in a fast-paced, diverse environment. You will be a nurturer of people: recognizing and growing the talent around you, exemplifying values of transparency, respect and innovation. You will be committed to learning, knowledge-sharing, convening and communicating with partners to work together to ideate, develop and implement climate action initiatives that make a profound difference to people and planet. You will join a team of talented, committed individuals representing almost 80 nationalities contributing skills and experience from academic, scientific, private, government and nonprofit backgrounds. Together, we work with governments, communities and civil society, technical agencies, and the private sector across the world. Interested in more information? Learn about working for GCF: https://www.greenclimate.fund/about/careers View current vacancies: https://jobs.greenclimate.fund/ About The Green Climate Fund (GCF) Set up in 2010 by the 194 countries who are Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), GCF takes its responsibility as the world’s largest dedicated multilateral climate fund to heart. GCF funds transformative climate projects across the developing world, supporting countries in their responses and actions to tackle climate change while fostering sustainable development within their communities. Our country-driven approach ensures that our actions are tailored to the unique circumstances and national aspirations of each nation we support. Besides channeling public and private sector investment through a broad range of financing instruments, GCF builds the capacity of developing countries to take climate action through an extensive Readiness Programme ensuring countries are increasingly well-equipped and financed to manage their climate futures. Headquartered in the Republic of Korea, GCF operates with a diverse and talented workforce of over 300 people. Department Introduction The Department of Information Technology (DIT) enables the Green Climate Fund's mission through secure, reliable, and innovative technology services. DIT oversees enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, digital workplace services, business applications, data and analytics platforms, and artificial intelligence adoption across the Secretariat. Working in partnership with business units, DIT drives digital transformation, strengthens data governance, modernizes business processes, and delivers technology solutions that improve operational efficiency, decision-making, and organizational resilience. As a strategic enabler, DIT ensures that technology, data, and AI are governed, sustainable, and aligned with GCF's institutional priorities and future growth. Role Summary The role serves as a primary liaison between the IT department and business units, ensuring that technology initiatives align with organizational goals. This position requires a high level of business acumen, technical expertise, and initiative to shape technology strategies that maximize business value. Responsibilities include business partnering, driving complex IT projects, and overseeing project management functions to ensure the successful execution and delivery of critical initiatives. The ideal candidate is proactive, solution-oriented, and adept at managing cross-functional collaboration. Duties And Responsibilities Understand the business strategic goals and translate them into technology solutions using technology and systems best practices. Advise business and IT leaders on new approaches that sustain the quality of IT services, projects, and products. Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with executive and senior management teams. Develop and maintain an in-depth understanding of business processes and challenges to proactively identify IT solutions. Influence technology adoption and digital transformation initiatives across the organization. Collaborate with IT leadership to develop roadmaps and strategies for technology adoption and optimization. Develop and execute project plans across a range of well-defined and established project elements aligned with broader organizational objectives. Monitor and analyze business unit performance to identify areas for improvement. Ensure that IT initiatives align with organizational objectives and deliver measurable value. Adapt project and programme initiatives, priorities, and methods in response to changing client needs and operational or technological conditions. Ensure IT governance for the department is aligned with organizational and departmental policies and standards. In collaboration with DIT colleagues, support and coordinate the financial management of IT costs and budget associated with business departments, ensuring transparency and accountability. Serve as the primary point of contact for IT requests, streamlining processes to eliminate duplication of efforts and enhance efficiency. Sustain project and programme relevance through seamless and comprehensive service to clients. Coordinate change management efforts to drive successful adoption of new systems and processes. Ensure transparent and timely communication with stakeholders throughout project lifecycles. Develop comprehensive training and support plans to facilitate smooth transitions and user adoption. Manage IT projects and programmes for the business teams, from inception to closure in collaboration with senior DIT members. Sustain delivery against established cycles and schedules, while incorporating new policies and procedures and evolving client needs. Develop detailed project plans, resource allocations, risk assessments, and contingency strategies in collaboration with senior DIT members. Maintain delivery schedules through varying conditions, resource constraints, and problematic client engagement. Coordinate with cross-functional teams, including developers, analysts, and business stakeholders. Manage cross-team communication to promote effective coordination of service delivery, ensuring priorities are aligned. Monitor project progress, resolve issues, and ensure that project objectives are met on time and within budget. Engage with stakeholders at all levels to provide updates, solicit feedback, and drive decision-making. Sustain quality of projects and programmes through adaptation to changing operational demands and client feedback. Champion project governance practices and ensure adherence to project management methodologies. Conduct thorough business analysis to understand requirements and assess the impact of proposed technology solutions, tailoring projects and programmes to reflect a thorough understanding of team capacities, organizational priorities, resources, client needs, and the operational and technological context. Implement quality assurance processes to ensure that solutions meet stakeholder expectations and industry standards. Facilitate testing and validation to maintain high-quality deliverables. Collaborate with technology vendors and service providers, ensuring service levels are maintained. In coordination with the Procurement team, support procurement processes to secure optimal terms and value. Conduct vendor and service-provider performance evaluations and implement measures to address any service gaps Requirements Master’s degree in computer science, electronics and communication, information systems; MBA or similar postgraduate business qualification, or a relevant bachelor’s degree with an additional two (2) years of professional experience. At least eight (8) years of professional experience in ICT project management implementation and service delivery, with at least five (5) years of experience working directly with senior business leaders. Proven track record of successfully managing complex, high-impact IT projects. Knowledge of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, and emerging technologies, including their application to business transformation, process optimization, data-driven decision-making, and innovation; experience with AI solutions and AI-enabled business initiatives is an asset. Knowledge of AI-assisted development and rapid application development approaches, including the use of AI-powered tools to enhance productivity, accelerate solution delivery, and support digital innovation, is an asset. Certification in project management, product management, or service management (e.g., PRINCE2, PMP, ITIL, Scrum) is highly desirable. Certification in the Governance of Enterprise IT is highly desirable. Certification in Risk and Information Systems Control is highly desirable. Proficiency in project and portfolio management tools. Strong business acumen, with knowledge of the operations of climate funds or comparable international financial institutions, is considered an asset. Fluent written and oral communication skills in English are essential for this position; knowledge of another UN language is an advantage. The closing date for applications is 22 November 2026. Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered. Applications from women and nationals of developing countries are strongly encouraged. The candidate assessed by the Selection Panel as most suitable for the position will be proposed for appointment. Selection among shortlisted candidates will also take into account performance at interview, appropriate testing, and references. Due to the high volume of applications we receive, only candidates under further consideration will be contacted. Candidates who are not selected for succeeding stages will be notified through the recruitment system once the selection process has been completed and the position has been filled. We encourage applicants to check the status of their applications regularly for updates. Staff members are subject to transfer or reassignment at the discretion of the Executive Director, in accordance with the Staff Regulations and Staff Rules. In the event of a transfer to another duty station, the staff member’s salary, allowances, benefits, and other applicable entitlements will be adjusted to reflect the conditions applicable at the new duty station, in accordance with the Staff Regulations and Staff Rules and other legal instruments in effect at the time of transfer. For details on grade levels, salary scales, and benefits, please refer to the GCF Staff Regulations and Staff Rules: https://www.greenclimate.fund/document/staff-regulations

review_candidates.description: Overview Jhpiego is a nonprofit global leader in the creation and delivery of transformative healthcare solutions for the developing world. In partnership with national governments, health experts, and local communities, we build health providers’ skills and we develop systems that save lives now and guarantee healthier futures for women and their families. We are seeking a dynamic Technical Assistant based in Homabay County to support the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of innovative service delivery approaches that strengthen health outcomes for mothers and children. The Technical Assistant will play a pivotal role in advancing innovative service delivery models to improve access to quality Maternal, Newborn, Child Health, Immunization, and Nutrition (MNCHIN) services, with a focus on strengthening maternal and newborn care, improving immunization coverage among children under five, particularly underserved populations such as zero-dose children, and supporting nutrition interventions for pregnant and breastfeeding women and children under five years of age. This role involves translating technical guidance into practical tools and processes, supporting onsite mentorship, and ensuring effective implementation at the facility level. The Technical Assistant will contribute to knowledge generation by drafting technical briefs, donor reports, and presentations, while actively participating in brainstorming sessions to test and refine new approaches. A key responsibility includes gathering insights from health facilities and documenting learnings to inform adaptive programming and continuous improvement. Responsibilities Collaborate with program leads and stakeholders to conceptualize and pilot new approaches that improve access to high-quality MNCHIN services, ensuring quality ANC, access to skilled delivery, and postnatal services. Use data, community feedback, and global best practices to inform design and scale-up of service delivery innovations. Support in delivering hands-on onsite mentorship to frontline health workers, supervisors, and facility staff. Translate complex technical guidelines into practical tools, workflows, and job aids that are usable and work on the ground. Monitor implementation and troubleshoot challenges in real time to ensure project effectiveness. Draft clear, compelling, and evidence-based documents including success stories that communicate program achievements, challenges, and lessons learned. Support the preparation of donor-facing materials, including quarterly reports, success stories, and strategic updates. Bring energy to brainstorming sessions, help test innovations, and feedback what’s working , and what’s not. Collect insights from health facilities and document learnings , to inform adaptive programming. Synthesize findings into actionable recommendations for program improvement and knowledge sharing. Required Qualifications Degree in nursing and/or midwifery, Clinical Medicine, or a related field. Current registration and valid practicing license with the relevant professional regulatory body, where required. Minimum 3 years’ experience in implementation of RMNCAH/ health programs Demonstrated practical experience in maternal and newborn care, child health, routine immunization and nutrition service delivery, mentorship or program implementation. Experience working with county and sub-county health management teams, health facilities, community health structures and implementing partners is desirable. Training or practical experience in Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care, Integrated Management of Newborn and Childhood Illness, Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition, Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition, immunization, quality improvement and/or respectful maternity care is desirable (EmONC, MIYCN, IMAM and IMNCI training is desirable) Experience preparing technical reports, presentations, implementation updates, success stories and other knowledge products. Good interpersonal skills and teamwork Ability to work with minimal supervision Excellent organizational skills including the ability to multitask Be of high integrity and able to maintain confidentiality. Strong presentation and communication skills, oral and written The deadline for applications is Monday 9th November 2026. Jhpiego offers competitive salaries and a comprehensive employee benefits package Please apply at www.jhpiego.org/careers Applicants must submit a single document for upload to include: cover letter, resume, and references. For further information about Jhpiego, visit our website at www.jhpiego.org Note: The successful candidate selected for this position will be subject to a pre-employment background investigation. Here in the UK we employ around 5,000 people across the country to deliver services that have a profound impact on people’s lives. From assessments and health services to employability programmes and specialist support, we do work that matters with people who care. You will be managing a team that will deliver Weight Management Services to the area, empowering local families to be healthier and happier. We want to build relationships with local families to learn: what they care about, what matters to them, what barriers they face and what strengths they have as individuals, families and communities. Key focus includes the referral management, personalised care pathways (aligned to need/preferences) and health coaching delivery. Sub-contractors and key partners Community stakeholders Co-location cooperatives Venue providers Healthcare settings including GP Practices / Primary Care Networks Qualifications & Experience Essential: Experience of a supervisory role with experience of managing a diverse team Relevant health coaching qualification or an accredited health coaching skills programme. Experience of coordinating health and wellbeing services Desirable: Experience in delivering behaviour change interventions for specific lifestyle related issues (smoking cessation, physical activity, NHS Health Checks, weight management, alcohol reduction) Membership of professional body (ICF, EMCC, AoC, UKHCA) Educated to degree level in a relevant subject e.g., Psychology, Behavioural Science etc Experience of supporting people remotely / telephonically / digitally Experience in community development in areas of deprivation, Project Management and Developing new services Individual Competencies Essential: Ability to motivate, manage and lead a diverse team Ability to forge good working relationships with external organisations Ability to react quickly to unforeseen circumstances A strong understanding of the social / wider determinants of health A strong understanding of population-based approaches including segmentation and risk stratification A strong understanding of behaviour change principles and methodology. Detailed knowledge of the core concepts and principles of personalisation, patient activation, health behaviour change, self-efficacy, intrinsic motivation, and assets-based approaches Detailed understanding of self-management support and associated techniques Advanced skills development incorporating practice, reflection and planning for the application of learning to practice.
